<thought>Based on the mass spectrum, the compound shows a dominant M peak at ~199 Da and an M+2 peak of similar intensity, indicating a single bromine atom (79Br/81Br isotopic pattern). A plausible formula matching this mass and containing one bromine is C₇H₅BrO₂, which corresponds to bromobenzoic acid (any bromobenzene‑carboxylic acid isomer). The SMILES for 4‑bromobenzoic acid is “O=C(O)c1ccc(Br)cc1”. This SMILES is valid and matches the observed mass and isotopic pattern.</thought>
<final_answer>O=C(O)c1ccc(Br)cc1</final_answer>
